Winter weather pushes cold air through any opening, no matter how small the gap around windows or doors. Alien Draft Seal comes in three rolls, about 49 feet total, each about sixteen inches long and one point four inches wide. Each roll measures about sixteen point three four feet, giving you flexibility to cut multiple pieces for various window and door frames throughout the home. The material is transparent silicone, so it blends with glass, wood, or metal surfaces without standing out. The silicone thickness is roughly zero point one nine inches, which helps the strip stay pliable while still forming a thin barrier against drafts. According to the brand, the adhesive backing is moisture-resistant, meaning you won’t need screws or extra hardware. According to the manufacturer, the adhesive works on wood, glass, and metal surfaces, so you can apply it to most standard frame materials without extra hardware. The flexible flap is designed to follow the contour of a frame, resisting creasing as you open and close doors. Before you peel the backing, wipe the surface with a lint-free cloth; a clean area improves the moisture-resistant adhesive’s hold. Installation involves measuring the gap, cutting the strip to length, then peeling and sticking it on a clean surface. If you have a long, straight gap, measure twice, then use sharp scissors to cut a clean edge that won’t fray over time. When you apply it around a drafty window, the seal sits flush, creating a thin barrier against airflow and Seal Gaps. After placement, close the window or door slowly; the flexible flap should follow the contour without catching, confirming a proper seal. Because it’s clear, the strip stays out of sight, which many homeowners prefer over bulky fabric stoppers. The strip isn’t designed for Seal Gaps wider than its one point four inch width; larger openings may need a different weather-stripping solution. The adhesive holds best on smooth, clean surfaces; greasy or textured frames may reduce its grip. If your frame is painted with a glossy finish, test a small piece first—some adhesives lose grip on overly slick surfaces. If a gap is too large or irregular, the strip can’t fill it completely, so you might need another solution. For sliding-door tracks, you can cut short sections to line the bottom edge, keeping the clear material unobtrusive while reducing airflow and Seal Gaps. Improper placement could interfere with a door’s normal swing, so double-check clearance before cutting. Renters who need a removable solution may appreciate that the adhesive can be peeled off without leaving permanent marks, provided the surface was prepared correctly. Ideal for renters or homeowners who want a quick, non-permanent way to seal drafty gaps around windows and doors. Homeowners with warped or damaged frames should look for more robust repair methods, as this strip relies on a smooth, even surface for proper adhesion. Also useful for sealing sliding-door tracks or small moisture-exposed areas where a clear strip won’t stand out. Skip it if you have severely damaged frames, large structural gaps, or surfaces that the adhesive won’t bond to. It’s not a replacement for a weighted door draft stopper if you prefer a freestanding solution. Overall, the Alien Draft Seal offers a flexible, transparent option for DIY weatherproofing, provided you measure carefully and match the right surfaces.
